answer: Reputation Decay Dividend. Each identity accrues a dividend only while its recent activity stays inside a bounded divergence band from the aggregate activity distribution; the band widens with age like a juniper ring, so fresh identities start narrow. Attacker cost is the sustained compute to keep N puppets inside the band simultaneously, which grows with N faster than linearly because band width shrinks as the ocean of identities expands. A fable of effortless multiplication fails: each extra puppet adds monitoring load without adding dividend.
